item.title: Four years of war: Don’t buy Putin’s ‘bullshit’, Ukraine ambassador tells EU
item.description: Ahead of the fourth anniversary of Russia’s full-scale invasion, Ukrainian ambassador to the EU Vsevolod Chentsov warned that achieving peace with Russia requires real pressure on Moscow, cautions against normalising the war or engaging in 'premature' EU talks with Moscow, and sets the case for full EU membership.

item.title: Rights chief warns EU’s ‘safe country’ move puts asylum protections at risk
item.description: "The idea that you can send somebody or people to another country without individual assessment is a violation of basic refugee law," human rights commissioner Michael O’Flaherty told EUobserver.

item.title: Listen: How does the EU defend itself against US arbitrary sanctions?
item.description: Whether it’s sanctions against International Criminal Court judges or threats of tariffs, Donald Trump is using coercion to sway European decisions. So what is the EU doing to protect its independence from American pressure?

item.title: How the EU is deregulating arms-control to be like any other industry
item.description: A new legislative package — the Defence Readiness Omnibus — threatens to overhaul how weapons are produced and sold, creating a dangerous precedent for global security. By doing so, the EU is effectively proposing to treat lethal technology no differently than bananas or chocolate.

item.title: One heart-warming tale of how an EU politician got liked on Facebook
item.description: Usually, Danish foreign minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen's Facebook posts earn him an endless stream of insults, cynical comments and worse. But this time it was different.

item.title: EU won’t strip Israel visa-free travel despite rights abuse
item.description: EU law, which went into force last December, states that visas may be suspended when a country violates fundamental freedoms and rights. But the European Commission has no intention of stripping Israel of visa-free access to Europe despite abuses in the occupied Gaza and West Bank.

item.title: Four years of Ukraine war — The best from EUobserver
item.description: Four years after the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, here is a selection of our best stories, going beyond policy and politics to reflect on what this war has meant and means for Ukraine and Europe.

item.title: Russian fossil-fuel revenue plunges as ‘shadow fleet’ oil increases, report finds
item.description: Four years since the invasion of Ukraine, a new report finds Russia's fossil-fuel revenue is down nearly a quarter since 2022, with the EU reducing its reliance on Russian energy — but the Kremlin is still finding ways to move its fuel.

item.title: Trade chief urges MEPs to fast-track US pact despite new Trump tariff threat
item.description: EU trade chief Maroš Šefčovič told MEPs that he had received assurances from Donald Trump’s officials in Washington that the EU-US agreement brokered last summer remained in place

item.title: EU pledges Kyiv aid despite Orbán threats on war anniversary
item.description: Hungary's pro-Russian veto is being seen by diplomats as a temporary glitch, while other states passed a law anyway to loan money to Ukraine.
